meta.source_authority: City of Mississauga â€“ Planning and Building Department, Building Division
meta.legislation: Ontario Building Code Act, S.O. 1992, c.23; Ontario Building Code O.Reg 332/12; Building By-Law 0236-2024; User Fees & Charges By-law 0221-2024
meta.notes: This list is not exhaustive. When in doubt, contact the City of Mississauga Building Division at 311 (905-615-4311 outside City limits) or visit mississauga.ca. Zoning By-law compliance is always required regardless of permit status. All applications must be submitted through the ePlans portal at eplans.mississauga.ca.

contact.address: 300 City Centre Drive, 3rd Floor, Mississauga, ON L5B 3C1
contact.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

common_forms.note: These forms appear on nearly every permit application. They are listed here once for reference and repeated in each rule's required_forms array with context-specific notes.

F-001.name: Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish
F-001.description: The primary building permit application form. Required for ALL permit submissions. Submitted through ePlans portal.

F-002.name: Applicable Law Form
F-002.description: Required for all permit applications. Indicates which additional approvals may be required for your project (heritage, conservation authority, MTO, site plan, etc.).

F-003.name: Schedule 1: Designer Information
F-003.description: Required for all permit applications where a designer (other than a homeowner) prepared the drawings. Must be signed and dated.

F-004.name: Schedule 1: Homeowner
F-004.description: Used when the homeowner is acting as their own designer/builder. Alternative to F-003 for owner-built projects.

F-005.name: SB-12 EEDS (Prescriptive) â€“ Energy Efficiency Design Summary
F-005.description: Required for new residential construction and additions to demonstrate energy efficiency compliance under Ontario Building Code Supplemental Standard SB-12.

F-006.name: SB-12 EEDS (Performance) â€“ Energy Efficiency Design Summary
F-006.description: Alternative to F-005 when using a performance-based energy compliance method.

F-007.name: Residential Mechanical Ventilation Design Summary Form
F-007.description: Required for new residential buildings and major additions. Documents mechanical ventilation design.

F-008.name: Single Dwelling Unit Information Letter
F-008.description: Required for new houses, garage conversions, basement finishes, additions, and below-grade entrances. Confirms single-unit status.

F-009.name: Roof Truss Layout Review Form
F-009.description: Required when engineered roof trusses are proposed. Documents truss system design.

F-010.name: Commitment to General Review
F-010.description: Required for non-residential projects. Confirms an architect/engineer will provide general review of construction.

F-011.name: Letter of Use
F-011.description: Required for all non-residential and ICI building permit applications and change of use applications. Describes the proposed use of the space.

F-012.name: Demolition Control Permit Declaration
F-012.description: Required for all residential demolition permit applications.

F-013.name: General Review Demolition Commitment Certificate
F-013.description: Required for non-residential demolition projects. Confirms architect/engineer oversight.

F-014.name: Residential Furnace Replacement Form (Datasheet)
F-014.description: Required specifically for residential furnace replacement permit applications.

F-015.name: Application to Register a Second Unit
F-015.description: Required when creating or legalizing a second residential unit (basement apartment, garden suite, etc.).

F-016.name: Water Service Pipe Sizing
F-016.description: Required for new houses, garage conversions, and units with three or more plumbing fixtures. Documents water service sizing calculations.

F-017.name: Schedule 2: Sewage System Installer Information
F-017.description: Required when the application involves sewage system work.

F-018.name: SB-10 ASHRAE 90.1 (Level 1) â€“ Non-Residential Energy
F-018.description: Energy efficiency compliance form for non-residential buildings using ASHRAE 90.1-2013 standard.

F-019.name: Supplementary Information Form
F-019.description: Required for new houses and non-residential buildings. Pages 1, 2, and 5 typically required for residential new builds.

fee_schedule.note: Fees shown are from the 2025 Building Division fee schedule. The 2026 fees are updated in Schedule B of the Building By-Law. Check mississauga.ca/publication/building-permit-fee-schedule/ for current rates.
fee_schedule.fee_formula: Permit Fee = SI (Service Index) x A (floor area in mÂ²)

pre_screen_fee.note: Non-refundable. Paid when submitting online through ePlans.

residential_part9.note: Minimum for residential projects within Division B, Part 9 of the Building Code. 2026 rate; 2025 rate was $237.

non_residential_or_part3.note: Minimum for non-residential and residential projects outside Division B, Part 9. 2026 rate; 2025 rate was $375.

service_index_rates.note: Service Index (SI) rates from 2025 schedule. Used in formula: Fee = SI x floor area (mÂ²).

conditional_permit_additional.note: 20% of permit fee, min $1,010 max $8,920. Each extension = $1,010.

payment_options.under_5000: Full fee at time of application
payment_options.5000_to_40000: Option A: Full fee at application. Option B: 50% at application, balance at permit issuance.
payment_options.over_40000: Option A: Full fee at application. Option B: Minimum $20,000 deposit at application, balance at permit issuance.

refund_policy.permit_issued: 45% refund, less 5% per inspection conducted. No refund after 6 months of permit issuance.

permit_required.description: Constructing any new residential or non-residential building, including new detached houses, garden suites, townhouses, semi-detached houses, and commercial/industrial buildings.
conditions: Any new building or structure over 10 sq m requires a permit.
Any new building of any size that contains plumbing requires a permit.
Garden suites (detached additional residential units) require a building permit.
Pre-approved garden suite plans (studio: 40 mÂ², one-bedroom: 55 mÂ²) are available to fast-track approval.

fee.effective: 2025 rates; check fee schedule for 2026 updates

required_forms.notes: Primary application form, submitted via ePlans.
Applicable Law Form required for all applications.
Schedule 1 Designer Information â€“ required when a designer prepares drawings.
SB-12 EEDS (Prescriptive) energy efficiency form for new residential Part 9 buildings.
Residential Mechanical Ventilation Design Summary Form.
Roof Truss Layout Review Form â€“ if engineered trusses proposed.
Application to Register a Second Unit â€“ if a secondary suite is included.

additional_approvals_possible: Ministry of Transportation Ontario (MTO) â€“ if within MTO controlled area
Committee of Adjustment (if zoning variances required)

permit_required.description: Adding floor area to an existing residential building, including rear additions, second-storey additions, side additions, sunrooms, and attached garages.
conditions: All additions to existing buildings require a permit.
Unheated additions (e.g., enclosed porch, sunroom without heating) are permitted but at a lower SI rate.
Deck, fireplace, and unfinished basement proposed at the same time as a new single-dwelling get no additional fee.

required_forms.notes: Residential Mechanical Ventilation Design Summary Form.
Roof Truss Layout Review Form â€“ if applicable.
Water Service Pipe Sizing â€“ if plumbing affected.

required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, property lines, setbacks, lot coverage, existing/proposed labels)
Floor plans (room dimensions, structural framing, smoke alarm/CO detector locations, plumbing, HVAC)
Roof plan (slopes, ventilation, rafter/truss specs)
Elevations for each side (grades, wall cladding, window/door locations, glazing percentages)

permit_required.description: Constructing a new deck, porch, or balcony attached to a residential property, or repairing/replacing guards on apartment/condo balconies.
conditions: A permit is required for any deck MORE THAN 0.61 m (2 feet) above grade.
Covered porches require a permit regardless of height.
Balcony construction, replacement, or guard repairs on apartments/condos require a permit.
Decks proposed at the same time as a new single dwelling unit have no additional fee.

fee.unit: Flat fee per deck/porch (min $244). Balcony guard: $17/linear m, max $1,784.

required_drawings: Site plan (scale, north arrow, property address, existing buildings labeled, proposed deck hatched/labeled 'PROPOSED', setbacks from all property lines, lot coverage calculations)
Floor plan (structural framing: size, type, grade, spacing, span direction of all structural members; section marks; soil bearing capacity; foundation size and material)
Roof plan if applicable (slopes, ventilation, skylight locations, rafter spacing)
Elevations for each side (grade level, existing/proposed work, finished floor levels, guard heights, roof overhang)

permit_required.project_type: Detached garage, shed (over 15 mÂ²), or accessory structure
permit_required.description: Constructing a new detached garage, carport, or shed exceeding 15 square metres, or any accessory structure containing plumbing.
conditions: Detached garages ALWAYS require a permit.
Sheds OVER 15 mÂ² (approximately 161 sq ft) require a permit.
Any shed or structure of ANY SIZE that contains plumbing requires a permit.
Gazebos over 10 mÂ² require a permit.
One-storey, free-standing sheds UNDER 15 mÂ² with no plumbing and used for storage only are EXEMPT.
Gazebos 10 mÂ² or smaller are EXEMPT.
Fee: Detached garage/shed as accessory to house is SI $6.24/mÂ² (min $244).
Demolition of accessory structure: flat fee $237.
required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, existing/proposed structures labeled, property line dimensions, setbacks, lot coverage calculations, driveway details)

Floor plan (north arrow, room dimensions, door/window sizes, structural framing details, floor drains, ventilation, foundation specs including soil bearing capacity, footing size/thickness/material, slab specs)
Roof plan (slopes, ventilation, rafter sizing and spacing)
Elevations for each side (grade level, existing/proposed work, finished floor levels, wall finishes, window/door locations, vertical dimensions to ridge/eaves, glazing percentages)

permit_required.project_type: Basement apartment / Second unit / Additional residential unit
permit_required.description: Creating a self-contained secondary suite within an existing home (basement apartment, in-law suite, garage conversion to unit), or adding an attached additional residential unit.
conditions: A building permit is required to create any second unit or basement apartment.
A second unit registration is also required â€” submit the Application to Register a Second Unit.
Property owners can add up to TWO additional residential units (ARUs) on detached, semi-detached, or townhome properties.
Building permit fees are FULLY REFUNDED when constructing or legalizing ARUs.
Second and third ARUs are exempt from most municipal charges (development charges).
Townhouses have restrictions; condominiums prohibit attached units without board approval.
Heritage properties may need Heritage Advisory Committee review.
Garden suites (detached ARUs): one permitted per lot, requires separate municipal address, 1.2m-wide x 2.1m-high emergency access pathway (max 45m from street).
Zoning regulations apply (setbacks, height, coverage) â€” verify using the city's property information tool.
Pre-approved garden suite plans available (studio 40 mÂ², one-bedroom 55 mÂ²) to expedite review.

fee.amount: SI $11.00/mÂ² plus minimum residential fee (2025 rate)
fee.incentive: Building permit fees FULLY REFUNDED for ARUs. Most municipal charges also waived.

required_forms.notes: Application to Register a Second Unit â€“ required for all second unit permits.
Water Service Pipe Sizing â€“ required for three or more units on the property.

required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, all structures labeled, dimensioned property lines, setbacks, lot coverage, GFA breakdown including second unit area, driveway details)

Floor plans (room uses/sizes, interior/exterior dimensions, legend distinguishing existing/demolished/proposed walls, structural framing, smoke alarms and CO detectors, plumbing fixtures, HVAC grille locations, cross-section details)
Elevations (if exterior changes) â€“ each side showing grade, wall cladding, window/door locations, glazing percentages

permit_required.description: Finishing an unfinished basement in a residential property (adding walls, rooms, bathroom, etc.) where it will NOT become a separate rental unit.
conditions: A permit is required for finishing a basement.
Fee is based on SI $5.48/mÂ² of finished basement area.
If the basement is being converted to a secondary suite/apartment, use PR-005 instead.
required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, existing structures labeled, dimensioned property lines, rights-of-way, easements, landscaping)

Floor plan (room uses/sizes, interior/exterior dimensions, door/window sizes, legend for existing/demolished/proposed walls, structural framing details, smoke alarm and CO detector locations, plumbing fixture locations existing/proposed, floor drains, ventilation, HVAC grille locations, section marks)

permit_required.description: Structural or mechanical changes to the interior of a residential building including removing/adding walls, changing room layouts, or modifying systems.
conditions: Interior alterations require a permit when structural work, plumbing, or mechanical changes are involved.
Purely cosmetic work (painting, flooring, cabinetry) does NOT require a permit.
Fee for residential interior alterations: SI $6.64/mÂ².
required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, existing structures, dimensioned property lines)

Floor plan (north arrow, room uses/sizes, interior/exterior dimensions, door/window sizes, legend for existing/demolished/proposed walls, structural framing details, smoke alarm and CO detector locations, plumbing fixture locations, floor drains, ventilation, HVAC grille locations)

permit_required.description: Complete demolition of a residential building or structure.
conditions: A permit is required to demolish any residential building.
Demolition of an accessory structure (garage, shed): flat fee $237.
Demolition of a house/ICI building: $22.00 per 100 mÂ² of Gross Floor Area demolished.
Property owners may qualify for tax reductions under Municipal Act Sections 357 and 358 â€” contact tax@mississauga.ca.
If work is done without a permit, an 'order to comply' may be issued; discharge fee is $600.

required_forms.notes: Demolition Control Permit Declaration â€“ required for all residential demolitions.

required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, legal description, existing structures labeled 'to be demolished' or 'existing to remain', dimensioned property lines, rights-of-way, easements)

permit_required.description: Complete demolition of a commercial, industrial, or institutional building.
conditions: A permit is required to demolish any non-residential building.
Fee: $22.00 per 100 mÂ² of GFA demolished (min $386).
Requires a General Review Demolition Commitment Certificate (architect/engineer oversight).
A Demolition Report must be submitted.
required_drawings: Site plan (property address, road location, dimensioned property lines, outline of existing structures to be demolished)

permit_required.description: Construction of a new retaining wall.
conditions: Retaining walls UNDER 1 metre high do NOT require a permit.
Retaining walls OVER 1 metre high require a permit.
Height threshold applies especially for walls on or adjacent to public property (streets, building entrances, private property accessible to the public).
Fee: $11.00 per linear metre.

permit_required.description: Creating a new below-grade entrance (exterior stairwell) to a basement or constructing a basement walkout.
conditions: A permit is required for any below-grade entrance or basement walkout.
Excavation of foundation walls (underpinning) also requires a permit.

fee.amount: $237.00 flat fee (same category as decks/porches to houses)

required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, legal description, existing structures, proposed entrance hatched and labeled 'PROPOSED', dimensioned property lines, setbacks from all property lines)

Floor plans (basement and ground floor) â€“ room uses, dimensions, legend for existing/demolished/proposed walls, floor drains, ventilation, section marks; basement must show soil bearing capacity, foundation wall/footing specs, step-down footing details, concrete slab and granular fill specs

permit_required.project_type: Residential exterior alterations (windows, doors, siding, roofing requiring structural changes, skylights)
permit_required.description: Changes to the exterior of a residential building including adding or enlarging windows/doors, installing skylights, re-cladding with new material, or alterations affecting roof height/slope.
conditions: NEW windows or doors require a permit.
ENLARGED windows or doors require a permit.
REPLACING windows or doors with the SAME SIZE does NOT require a permit.
Re-cladding with DIFFERENT materials requires a permit.
Re-cladding with the SAME material does NOT require a permit.
Re-shingling a roof (like-for-like) does NOT require a permit.
Roof EXTENSIONS or alterations that change height or slope require a permit.
Skylights require a permit.
Dormers require a permit.
required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, property dimensions, legal description, existing/proposed structures labeled, setbacks)
Floor plan (structural framing details, door/window sizes, section marks)
Elevations for each side of the project (grade levels, finished floor levels, exterior finishes, roof slope, window/door locations, glazing percentage relative to exposed wall)

permit_required.description: Converting an attached or detached garage into a habitable residential space or self-contained unit.
conditions: A permit is required for all garage conversions to residential use.
Heat loss calculations and mechanical ventilation design are required.
If converting to a secondary suite, also register the second unit.

required_forms.notes: Residential Mechanical Ventilation Design Summary Form.

required_drawings: Site plan (metric scale, north arrow, address, legal description, existing/proposed structures, lot coverage, site statistics including garage area, driveway yard dimensions, landscaped percentages)
Floor plans (room dimensions, door/window sizes, structural framing, smoke alarm/CO detector locations, plumbing fixture locations, HVAC grille positions)
Roof plans (slopes, ventilation, skylight locations, rafter/truss specs)
Elevations if exterior changes occur (grade level, existing/proposed work, finished floor heights)

permit_required.description: Installation or replacement of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems including furnaces, boilers, heat pumps, geothermal systems, and independent HVAC work.
conditions: Furnace replacement (higher efficiency model or different fuel type) requires a permit.
Altering furnace ducts requires a permit.
Rooftop HVAC replacement requires a permit.
HVAC unit installation (unit heater, rooftop unit, make-up air unit) requires a permit.
Full heating system replacement requires a permit.
Geothermal systems require a permit.
Solar thermal (hot water) systems require a permit.
Kitchen exhaust systems require a permit.
Commercial kitchen exhaust: $416 flat fee.
Spray booth: $416/unit.
Like-for-like furnace filter or thermostat replacement does NOT require a permit.

required_forms.notes: Residential Furnace Replacement Form (Datasheet) â€“ required for furnace replacements.

conditional_documents: Heat Loss Calculations â€“ required only if making alterations to ducts
HVAC Sample Drawing â€“ required only if making alterations to ducts

permit_required.description: Adding, removing, or relocating plumbing fixtures; installing or repairing drainage systems, backwater valves, backflow preventers, or private sewage systems.
conditions: Adding, removing, or relocating plumbing fixtures requires a permit.
Replacing existing plumbing fixtures in the SAME LOCATION does NOT require a permit.
Plumbing drainage installation or repair requires a permit.
Backflow preventers require a permit.
Backwater valves require a permit.
Private sewage system installation/repair/replacement requires a permit.
Sewer system work requires a permit.
Sump pump installation does NOT require a permit.
Fee: $41 per plumbing fixture; $1.65/linear m inside piping; $4.59/linear m outside piping.

permit_required.description: Installation of a new wood-burning fireplace, wood stove, or gas fireplace used for heating; installation or reconstruction of a chimney.
conditions: Wood-burning fireplaces require a permit.
Wood stoves require a permit.
Gas fireplaces used for HEATING require a permit.
DECORATIVE gas fireplaces (not used for heating) do NOT require a permit.
Installing or reconstructing a chimney or fireplace requires a permit.
Fee: $237.00 flat fee per fireplace/wood stove.
Fireplaces proposed at the same time as a new single-dwelling unit have no additional permit fee.

permit_required.description: Installation of solar panels (photovoltaic) or solar thermal collectors on a residential or non-residential building.
conditions: Solar panels and solar collector systems require a building permit.
Fee for a house: $309.00 flat fee.
Fee for non-residential/other than a house: $684.00 flat fee.

permit_required.description: Installation of fire alarm systems, fire suppression systems, sprinkler systems, or repairs to fire-damaged buildings.
conditions: Fire alarm systems require a permit: $774.00 flat fee.
Fire suppression systems require a permit: $416.00 flat fee.
Sprinkler systems require a permit.
Fire damage repairs require a permit.
Generators connected to life safety equipment require a permit.
Electromagnetic locks (maglocks) require a permit: $309/each, max $1,783.
For fire inspections: email fire.prevention@mississauga.ca or call 905-896-5908.

permit_required.description: Changing the occupancy or use of a building or part of a building (e.g., converting residential to commercial, or changing between commercial occupancy types).
conditions: A permit is required when the change of use represents an increase in hazard as defined by Ontario Building Code Article 1.3.1.4.

Triggered by: change of major occupancy designated in OBC Table 1.3.1.4; converting a Group C suite to more than one Group C suite; converting to gaming premises; changing to a post-disaster building; changing to a retirement home; changing from/to a farm building; change where previous use cannot be determined.
Exempt if: the change in use results from construction already covered under a Section 8 permit.
A Zoning Certificate of Occupancy is also required to approve the change of use.
A Letter of Use must be submitted with all non-residential permit applications.
Fee: Residential interior alteration rate SI $6.64/mÂ² or non-residential alteration rate.

fee.amount: SI $6.64/mÂ² for interior alterations (min $386 for non-residential)

required_forms.notes: Commitment to General Review â€“ for non-residential projects.
Letter of Use â€“ required for all non-residential and change of use applications.

permit_required.description: Installing a new roof, replacing a roof structure, or roof alterations that change the height or slope.
conditions: Re-SHINGLING (like-for-like replacement of shingles) does NOT require a permit.
New roof construction requires a permit.
Roof MEMBRANE replacement requires a permit.
Roof EXTENSIONS or structural alterations affecting height or slope require a permit.
Fee: SI $5.48/mÂ² for new roof or replacement; $4.88/mÂ² for roof membrane replacement.

permit_required.project_type: Non-residential new building, addition, or alteration
permit_required.description: New commercial, industrial, or institutional construction; additions to non-residential buildings; interior or exterior alterations to commercial/industrial/institutional spaces.
conditions: All new non-residential buildings require a permit.
All additions to non-residential buildings require a permit.
Interior and exterior alterations require a permit.
Drawings must be signed, sealed, and dated by an architect, professional engineer, and/or qualified designer.
A Commitment to General Review is required.
A Letter of Use must be included.
Minimum fee: $386 for non-residential projects.

required_forms.notes: SB-10 energy efficiency form for non-residential.

required_drawings: Site plan (metric, north arrow, address, legal description, existing/proposed structures, parking specs, lot area/frontage, GFA by floor, parking count)
Architectural drawings (room uses, fire separations, partition/door schedules)
Structural drawings (design criteria)
HVAC drawings (distribution system plans, duct sizes, damper locations)
Plumbing drawings (fixture locations, drain pipe sizing)
Electrical drawings (exit signs, emergency lights, fire alarm, full layout by licensed engineer)
Sprinkler drawings (shop-quality with hydraulic calculations)
Elevations for each side (grade, finishes, window/door locations, glazing percentages)

permit_not_required.description: Interior painting, wallpapering, or other purely decorative work.
conditions: No structural, plumbing, or mechanical changes involved.

permit_not_required.description: Replacing flooring, installing cabinetry or cupboards.
conditions: No structural modifications. Cabinets and cupboards in same location.

permit_not_required.description: Replacing existing windows or doors with new units of the same size and in the same location.
conditions: Must be same size and same location.
NEW windows/doors or ENLARGED openings DO require a permit.
Like-for-like replacement only.

permit_not_required.description: Replacing a toilet, sink, bathtub, or other plumbing fixture in the exact same location without changing drainage.
conditions: Must be same location â€” no relocation of fixtures.
Adding, removing, or relocating fixtures DOES require a permit.

permit_not_required.description: Building or replacing a residential fence.
conditions: Building permits are generally NOT required for residential fences in Mississauga.
Zoning and Fence By-law requirements still apply (max 2m rear/side yard, max 1m front yard closed, max 1.5m front yard open).
Fences cannot be made of barbed wire or hazardous materials.
Cannot be built on City property, highways, or road allowances.
Corner lot and sight triangle restrictions apply.
For non-compliant fences, apply for a fence exemption through Licensing, Permits & Regulatory Services.

permit_not_required.description: Constructing a low-level deck or platform that is 600 mm or less above finished grade.
conditions: Must be less than 0.61 m (approximately 2 feet) above finished grade.
Decks over 0.61 m high DO require a permit.
Zoning regulations (setbacks, lot coverage) still apply.

permit_not_required.description: A free-standing, one-storey storage shed under 15 square metres with no plumbing.
conditions: Must be under 15 mÂ² (approximately 161 sq ft) in floor area.
Must be single-storey.
Must be free-standing (not attached to house or other structure).
Must NOT contain any plumbing.
Must be used for storage only.
Sheds over 15 mÂ² OR containing plumbing DO require a permit.
Detached garages ALWAYS require a permit.
Zoning regulations (setbacks, coverage) still apply.

permit_not_required.description: Installing a prefabricated or built gazebo that is 10 square metres or smaller.
conditions: Must be 10 mÂ² or smaller.
Gazebos OVER 10 mÂ² DO require a permit.
Zoning regulations still apply.

permit_not_required.description: Replacing asphalt shingles or other roofing material with the same type of material on an existing roof.
conditions: Must be same material â€” like-for-like replacement.
No structural changes to roof framing.
Roof EXTENSIONS or changes to height/slope DO require a permit.
New roofing (different material or new structure) may require a permit.

permit_not_required.description: Replacing exterior cladding or siding with the exact same material.
conditions: Must be the same material.
Re-cladding with DIFFERENT materials DOES require a permit.
Structural changes to wall assembly may require a permit.

permit_not_required.description: Building a retaining wall less than 1 metre (approximately 3 feet 3 inches) in height.
conditions: Must be less than 1 metre in height.
Retaining walls OVER 1 metre high DO require a permit.
Zoning regulations still apply.

permit_not_required.description: Installing a decorative gas fireplace that is not used for heating purposes.
conditions: Must be purely decorative â€” not a primary or supplementary heat source.
Gas fireplaces used for HEATING DO require a permit.
Wood-burning fireplaces ALWAYS require a permit.
Gas connections may require separate gas contractor permit/inspection under TSSA.

permit_not_required.description: Repaving, resurfacing, or widening an existing driveway.
conditions: Building permit not required.
Driveway widening must still comply with zoning by-law (minimum landscaping requirements).
If adding a new catch basin or drainage structure, a permit may be required.

permit_not_required.description: General landscaping work including planting, grading, gardening.
conditions: Building permit not required for general landscaping.
Significant grade changes near structures may affect drainage and zoning compliance.
Zoning regulations still apply.

permit_not_required.description: Pouring a concrete pad or patio at grade level.
conditions: Building permit not required for a basic concrete pad.
If the pad supports a structure requiring a permit, the permit for the structure would apply.
Must comply with zoning setback requirements.

permit_not_required.description: Tuckpointing, repointing mortar joints, or minor brick repair.
conditions: Must be minor/cosmetic repair only.
Structural masonry work or significant recladding may require a permit.

permit_not_required.description: Installing or replacing eavestroughs and downspouts where drainage is contained on the property.
conditions: Drainage must remain on private property.
If connecting to external drainage systems with catch basins, a permit may be required.

permit_not_required.description: Installing a sump pump in an existing sump pit.
conditions: Sump pump installation does NOT require a permit.
If installing a NEW sump pit (excavation, new drain connections), a permit may be required.

permit_not_required.description: Applying waterproofing or damp-proofing to exterior basement walls.
conditions: Does not require a permit.
If excavation or foundation work is involved, a permit may be required.

permit_not_required.project_type: Insulation (existing wall/attic â€” same location, no vapour barrier changes)
permit_not_required.description: Adding insulation to existing walls, attic, or crawlspace without structural changes.
conditions: Adding insulation to existing spaces generally does not require a permit.
If the insulation work requires opening walls for structural changes or new vapour barriers as part of an alteration, a permit may be required for the broader renovation.
Insulation as part of a re-clad or addition does require a permit.

inspection_process.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
inspection_process.note: Schedule inspection BEFORE covering work with insulation, drywall, gravel, concrete, or other materials.

types.name: HVAC Inspection
checks: Return air register placement per approved drawings

types.name: Framing Inspection
checks: Prior rough-in inspections completed and passed

preparation: Post the building permit card visibly on site
Have all permit documents and approved drawings on site (colour, min 11Ã—17 inch)
Ensure previous stage inspections are passed before requesting next
Maintain inspector access to all areas of work

processing_times.note: Incomplete applications and resubmissions fall outside standard timelines and may add 2+ weeks per resubmission cycle.
